"Russia's Yandex says data centre in Vladimir shut down after drone attack"
Standfirst: "Third strike on Yandex facilities in a week comes as Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks on tech infrastructure."
BYLINE: "By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters" - AFP and Reuters attribution. Photo credit: Reuters (file, 8 October).

A Russian data centre run by technology and AI company YANDEX was shut down after a drone attack. No injuries reported in the attack on the facility in the city of VLADIMIR, east of Moscow, the company said on Sunday.
Emergency services were at the site and several Yandex services were unavailable to users as it evaluated ways to restore systems.
"Operations at the data centre have been completely suspended," Yandex said in a service alert on Telegram, advising users to activate disaster-recovery plans as the platform operated in emergency mode.
"The remaining resource configuration is considered unstable," it added, warning technical support communications could also be disrupted.
THIRD ATTACK on the company's data centres in the last week.
- FRIDAY: Yandex said its data centre in the KALUGA region southwest of Moscow was struck by Ukrainian drones and partly put out of action.
- A DAY EARLIER (Thursday): a Ukrainian attack shut down Yandex's data hub in SASOVO, southeast of Moscow, "where two of the three supercomputers used to develop the company's AI model are housed". Photo caption: the Sasovo hub is "one of the company's five large data centres" and "hosts tens of thousands of servers".
Yandex "is heavily involved in Russia's AI development and is sometimes referred to as 'Russia's Google'".
